Opening · The Bylaw One Guide

Bengaluru's building rules. One code.

Bengaluru's building rules. One code. Every building in Bengaluru is governed by 16 in-force instruments from 10 statutory bodies — municipal building bye-laws, master plan zoning regulations, dated gazette amendments, corporation notifications, and state Acts — current as of 14 May 2026.

Bylaw One joins those scattered official PDFs into one readable, cited, machine-readable building code. Nothing inside the legal text is rewritten or invented; every provision and table row links directly to the exact page of the official government PDF and its Internet Archive snapshot.

Slide summary: Bengaluru's building rules sit across 16 official instruments from 10 bodies. Bylaw One joins them into one open, cited, machine-readable code — 5,480 provisions, 271 rules as data, and 369 wards — current as of 14 May 2026.

Presenter notes: Welcome to Bylaw One. Look at any building plot in Bengaluru: the rules that govern it are not in a single book. They sit across 16 in-force acts, building bye-laws, master plan zoning regulations, and gazette amendments issued by 10 bodies over twenty-two years. Bylaw One joins those official publications into one open, cited, machine-readable code. Today the working pilot covers 5,480 structured provisions, 271 governing parameter rules as data, 5 City Corporations, 369 official wards, and 1,276 georeferenced land-use zone polygons across 4 sheets (1.5% of Greater Bengaluru), verified by 10 automatic checks on every build.

01 / The Narrative

1. Why this exists

Every building in India is governed by rules scattered across bye-laws, master plans, amendments, circulars and state Acts, published as PDFs by different bodies, often contradicting each other. Architects, engineers, students and homeowners spend days finding which rule applies, and still aren't sure. Bylaw One turns those rules into one open, cited, machine-readable code, so that any person, and any AI they use, can answer "what may I build here?" with the exact official page behind every answer. Built openly, verified by colleges and practitioners, starting with Bengaluru.

Bylaw One is built around three ideas:

  • Open — free data, free tools, no lock-in to any company, including AI companies.
  • Cited — every answer leads to the government's own page.
  • Collective — a city at a time, a state at a time, built and checked by the profession itself.

Closing line: Read. Trace. Compare.

02 / Live Walkthrough

2. See it working

Four live workflows show how the pilot works in practice today:

  1. The FAR story: Traces Floor Area Ratio across twenty-two years in five steps — 2004 (Building Bye-laws 2003, Bye-law 9.2: "The set backs required on all the sides of building/s, maximum plot coverage, maximum FAR, maximum number of floors, maximum height of buildings that are permissible for different dimensioned sites and widths of roads are set out in Tables 4, 5 and 6 given below.", p. 21), 2007 (Revised Master Plan 2015 Zoning Regulations, Chapter 4, Table 10, p. 28), 2017 (Bye-law 1.4 inserted by Notification UDD 14 TTP 2017, p. 2, handing use, coverage, FAR, setbacks, height, storeys, dwelling units, and parking to the Master Plan), 2025 (Premium FAR Chapter 11, Table 27, p. 2), and Today (how Base FAR, Premium FAR, and TDR combine under Note 2, p. 3).
  2. A subject page: Opens with What applies today (271 active parameter rows across subjects, with plain-word conditions, normal units m, m², %, and p. N PDF links), followed by Why this rule applies (with quoted statutory authority on tap) and collapsed Older or replaced rules.
  3. The map Place Card: Search any neighbourhood or ward (MiniSearch over 2,174 indexed places and 369 wards) to open the Place Card showing the Corporation, Ward, Planning district, Land-use zone, and Rules for this zone grouped into Uses, FAR, Ground coverage, Setbacks, Height, and Parking.
  4. A verification task: Shows the structured record on one side and an Open official page link on the other so students and practitioners can record Match, Mismatch, or Can't tell verdicts in the browser and export a .csv file.

03 / Pipeline, Resolution, Map & AI

3. How it's built

Bylaw One processes official regulations through seven verifiable stages:

  • Sources: Each of the 28 registered sources (16 in force) carries an HTTP retrieval record, SHA-256 checksum, Wayback Machine archive link, explicit instrument_type, and quoted status evidence.
  • Structure: 5,480 active provisions are structured in the law's own hierarchy (max depth <= 6) with Akoma Ntoso eid addresses and table rows. Site explanations live in separate notes_by_site fields so verbatim legal text is never altered.
  • Rules as data: Development-control tables are extracted into 271 active parameter records (313 total) across 10 parameter kinds with normalized units (m, m², %), numeric intervals, and cell-level page citations.
  • Settling overlaps: When instruments overlap, a stated six-step statutory order decides: (1) drafts never apply; (2) corporation amendments apply within that corporation; (3) the enabling Act prevails (Section 230); (4) Bye-law 1.4 hands zoning parameters to the Master Plan; (5) a later in-force amendment supersedes an earlier one; (6) unresolved ties are shown side by side as not settled.
  • Checks (10 per build): Every build checks text fidelity against stored PDF page text (data/page_text/), hierarchy depth, parameter plausibility bounds, table band continuity (3.1(ii) and 3.1(iii) for the 11.5 m–12 m setback band), 5-corporation parity, map street-offset (~8 m median, ~21 m 90th-percentile), R15/R16 provenance, plain-language gates, permissive licences (gitleaks + Rule R4), and WCAG 2.2 AA / page budgets. Two independent human Match verdicts are required before a record is marked Verified by a person.
  • The map: Built with MapLibre GL JS and @protomaps/basemaps (light) over basemap.pmtiles, layering 1,276 land-use zone polygons (4 sheets, 1.5% of Greater Bengaluru), a diagonal hatch over uncovered areas, planning districts, 369 wards, 5 corporations, and derived lake buffers.
  • Machines and AI: Today the site publishes /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt, .md mirrors for every document, subject, and provision page, a static JSON API at /api/v1/ (openapi.json), schema.org/Legislation JSON-LD, datapackage.json, and /updates.xml.
Details · Slide summary & presenter notes

Slide summary: Official PDFs pass through five deterministic layers — source register, verbatim structure, rules as data, six-step statutory resolution, and static web/AI endpoints — guarded by 10 automatic build checks and double-keyed human verification.

Presenter notes: How do we turn scanned and digital government PDFs into a trustworthy code? Every release passes through five layers. First, the source register acquires each official PDF with its SHA-256 digest, Wayback Machine snapshot, and quoted commencement evidence. Second, the structure stage builds a faithful hierarchy of 5,480 active provisions with tables as structured rows and keeps editorial summaries strictly separate in `notes_by_site`. Third, parameter extraction turns tables into 271 active condition-bearing records with cell-level provenance. Fourth, a stated six-step statutory order settles overlaps across instruments while keeping older rules visible. Fifth, the build publishes the web reader, the 8-layer Protomaps/MapLibre map, and machine-readable endpoints (`/llms.txt`, `.md` pages, `/api/v1/` OpenAPI 3.1 JSON). Every build runs 10 automatic verification suites, and records become "Verified by a person" only after two independent workshop Match verdicts.

04 / Non-Negotiable Rules

4. Principles

Six principles govern every dataset, map layer, and interface view in Bylaw One:

  • The law's words exactly as printed; nothing added inside legal text. Summaries and explanations sit outside the legal text and are labelled "In short, by this site" or "Note by this site". Every provision and home-page quote is checked in CI against the extracted text of its cited PDF page.
  • Every rule traced to its official page, with an archived copy. Every provision, parameter cell, and resolution step links to #page=N of the official Gazette, development authority, or municipal PDF alongside a Wayback Machine snapshot and SHA-256 digest.
  • Anything the site works out is labelled as derived. Consolidated "as amended" views, extracted parameter rows, statutory resolution chains, georeferenced land-use zones, and buffer overlays carry derived: true and are visibly labelled on the page.
  • When rules disagree, a stated order decides, and both rules stay visible; "not settled" when the law does not decide. Superseded and municipal provisions remain inspectable under "Older or replaced rules", and genuine ties are shown side by side rather than guessed.
  • Not legal advice; confirm with the authority. Bylaw One is an open public reference worked out from official documents; building approvals and plot decisions must be confirmed with the planning authority or a qualified professional.
  • Released data and code stay open permanently (code Apache-2.0, data CC BY 4.0). Underlying statutes, rules, regulations, bye-laws, and gazette notifications are public government works under Section 52(1)(q) of the Indian Copyright Act 1957.
Details · Slide summary & presenter notes

Slide summary: Six principles govern every release: verbatim legal text with nothing added inside, every rule traced to its official and archived page, derived values labelled, disagreements settled by stated order, not legal advice, and permanent openness (Apache-2.0 and CC BY 4.0).

Presenter notes: Every contributor, college steward, and AI integration in Bylaw One is bound by six plain principles. First, the law's words are shown exactly as printed, with nothing added inside legal text. Second, every rule is traced to its official page, with an archived copy. Third, anything the site works out — whether a consolidated provision, an extracted table row, or a 30-metre lake buffer — is explicitly labelled as derived. Fourth, when rules disagree, a stated order decides, and both rules stay visible; we show "not settled" when the law does not decide. Fifth, this is an open reference, not legal advice — always confirm with the authority. Sixth, released data and code stay open permanently under Apache-2.0 and CC BY 4.0.

05 / Roles, Layered Packs & State Stewards

5. The movement

How the work is organised

  • State stewards: colleges that curate their state's rules, verify records and teach with them.
  • Contributors: anyone proposing sources, corrections or cities.
  • Reviewers: faculty and practitioners who sign off verification.
  • Maintainers: the core team that runs the engine, data format and checks.
  • Bylaw One is run as a brand under [Owner's Organisation]; released work stays open regardless (code under Apache-2.0, data under CC BY 4.0).

Layered packs (planned)

Rules will be published as downloadable packs (planned): national, state and city. Shared text is stored once. Each layer records how it relates to the one above:

  1. Adopted: A state or city notification brings the higher-tier provision into force verbatim.
  2. Adopted with changes: A state or city notification adopts a model rule (such as Bye-law 1.4 from the 2017 notification or a corporation-specific Schedule-IV table) with local substitutions or conditions.
  3. Reference only: A national model or standard (such as the National Building Code 2016 or the 2017 Model Building Bye-laws issued under the Municipalities Act 1964) is recorded for cross-reference because a national or state model only applies where a state or city adopted it.

A city pack shows each rule's complete trail from national or state authority down to the municipal corporation.

Details · Slide summary & presenter notes

Slide summary: Bylaw One is organised around four roles — State stewards, Contributors, Reviewers, and Maintainers — and a planned three-tier pack architecture (national, state, and city) that records whether each higher rule is adopted, adopted with changes, or reference only.

Presenter notes: No single team can curate and verify the building rules of every Indian city alone. Bylaw One is organised as a collective movement across four clear roles: State stewards (colleges that curate their state's rules, verify records, and teach with them), Contributors (anyone proposing sources, corrections, or cities), Reviewers (faculty and practitioners who sign off verification), and Maintainers (the core team that runs the engine, data format, and checks). Bylaw One is run as a brand under the owner's organisation, and all released work stays open regardless. To scale across India without duplicating text, we have designed a planned layered pack architecture — national, state, and city — where shared text is stored once and each city pack records whether a state or national model rule was adopted, adopted with changes, or is reference only.

06 / Colleges, Students, Practitioners & Workshops

6. Take part

Why colleges, students and practitioners take part

  • Colleges: accreditation counts functional MoUs, meaning MoUs with real activity during the assessment period. Bylaw One's MoU comes with activities every semester: a one-day workshop, a faculty session, supervised verification internships. Plus a citable dataset and the state-steward role.
  • Students: skills employers want (reading city rules; using AI responsibly and checking it against the gazette); 60 to 120-hour verification internships that many universities can count toward internship credit; certificates; named credit in every release; a possible national student design trophy (designing within real, cited rules of a real site).
  • Faculty: publishable research and thesis material; citable releases.
  • Practitioners: hours saved finding which rule applies; early access to the planned agent engine; a voice in what comes next.
  • Civic and data groups: a shared, open, cited source.
  • How credit works: A record becomes Verified by a person only after at least two independent verifiers record a Match verdict with zero Mismatch verdicts. Every verifier's name, institution, and date are shown on the provision (Details) and listed in manifest.json and datapackage.json.

The workshop (one day)

  1. Why rules are hard: one plot, many documents (45 min).
  2. Follow one rule: the FAR story with the real documents (60 min).
  3. Verify for real: each student checks rules against official pages using the Verify page (90 min).
  4. AI with citations: ask an AI, check its answer against the page (60 min).
  5. Show and tell: findings, errors caught, certificates (30 min).

Also offered as a two-hour faculty session.

07 / Architecture, Pipeline & Planned Agent Engine

7. For developers

Repository layout, data model & running the pipeline

  • Repository layout: schemas/ (15 Draft 2020-12 JSON Schemas), jurisdictions/ (declarative YAML configs), data/overrides/<id>/ (committed OCR corrections, table overrides, zone tags, and workshop verifications), data/page_text/ (SHA-256-verified per-page text store), pipeline/ (uv-managed Python CLI bylaws), and app/, components/, lib/ (Next.js App Router web reader).
  • Data model: Three layers — Layer 1 faithful provision trees (clauses.json / per-chapter outlines), Layer 2 stand-off annotations (annotations.json), and Layer 3 dated amendment effects (amendments.json, consolidated.json, parameters.json, resolution.yaml, relations.json).
  • Running the pipeline & adding a source or city: Run uv run bylaws <stage> --jurisdiction <id> (acquire → parse → structure → amendments → parameters → relations → geo → apply-overrides → validate → publish). Adding a source or a new city requires only declarative entries in jurisdictions/<id>.yaml and data/overrides/<id>/ — zero city names or zone codes are ever hard-coded in Python or TypeScript (Rule R1).
  • Contribution rules: Permissive dependencies only (Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD — Rule R4), immutable raw sources (Rule R5), deterministic builds (Rule R6), and zero invented legal text (test_text_fidelity.py).

The planned pack format & agent engine (planned, for the launch)

  • Planned pack format: Downloadable national, state, and city packs (planned) storing shared text once and recording adopted, adopted with changes, or reference only links between layers.
  • One small engine (planned): Written in TypeScript, running on the user's own machine; data packs installed separately and updated as new rules are added.
  • Four doors (planned): (1) a local MCP server (for Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, Codex and other MCP apps); (2) a command line for any agent that can run commands; (3) an Agent Skill that teaches any agent the honesty rules (cite the page, label derived values, ask for missing plot details, confirm with the authority); (4) the open data files themselves.
  • Offline search & planned tools: Keyword search built in and meaning-based search with a small bundled model (planned). Planned tools: search rules; get a provision; resolve a plot (asks for missing dimensions instead of guessing); what changed; compare places; get sources.
  • Planned installation: Planned as a one-click bundle for AI desktop apps and native installers for Windows, macOS and Linux. A hosted endpoint for ChatGPT and web assistants comes later. (Install steps will be published only when the engine and installers ship; until then, see Use with AI for /llms.txt, .md pages, and /api/v1/.)
Details · Slide summary & presenter notes

Slide summary: The repository separates a Python data pipeline (`pipeline/`) from a static Next.js reader (`app/`) across 15 JSON Schemas (`schemas/`). A planned local TypeScript agent engine will expose four doors: MCP server, CLI, Agent Skill, and open data files.

Presenter notes: For developers and technical contributors, the repository has a clean two-half architecture. The offline Python 3.12+ pipeline (`pipeline/`, managed with `uv`) acquires PDFs, parses tables, structures provisions, applies amendments, extracts parameters, georeferences map sheets, and validates outputs against fifteen Draft 2020-12 JSON Schemas in `schemas/`. The Next.js App Router frontend at the repository root (`app/`, `components/`, `lib/`) is a static, read-only reader with zero city-specific constants (Rule R1). We are also designing the planned local agent engine for the launch: one small TypeScript engine running on the user's own machine with separately updated data packs, offline keyword and meaning-based search, and four doors — a local MCP server, a CLI, an Agent Skill teaching the honesty rules, and the open data files themselves.

10 / Declared Coverage Gaps & Roadmap

10. What's missing and what's next

What is missing today (from declarations.json)

Every coverage gap is declared openly on the Pilot page:

  • Land-use zone polygons (4 sheets, 1.5% of Greater Bengaluru): Currently cover 1,276 zone polygons in Planning Districts 2.10 Jayanagar and 2.11 Banashankari in Bengaluru South; uncovered areas on the map are marked with a diagonal hatch ("Land-use data not yet available").
  • July 2025 zoning amendment (UDD 85 MNJ 2025): The official gazette PDF could not be obtained from public sources (direct download returns HTTP 403 and no Wayback Machine snapshot exists), so consolidated zoning text and parameter values may not reflect changes made in July 2025.
  • October 2024 Kannada compilation: Published in Kannada only as an convenience compilation and not structured; this dataset uses the English original together with the 8 structured English amending notifications.
  • Supporting & reference-only instruments: Karnataka Fire and Emergency Services NOC rules, standalone TDR procedural rules, and Occupancy Certificate exemption orders are not yet in the dataset; the National Building Code of India 2016 (copyrighted by BIS) and Airports Authority of India NOCAS colour-coded zoning map are listed as reference only (Rule R13).

What comes next

  1. Bengaluru complete: Georeferencing and extracting the remaining RMP 2015 land-use sheets across all 5 City Corporations, acquiring remaining notifications, and running student and practitioner verification workshops.
  2. Karnataka: Extending the same schema and pipeline across urban development authorities and municipal corporations in Karnataka.
  3. Other states: Partnering with colleges of architecture, planning, and law as state stewards to bring other Indian cities and states into Bylaw One.
  4. Local agent engine (planned): Shipping the planned local MCP server, CLI, and Agent Skill so practitioners can run cited rule checks inside their own tools.
Details · Slide summary & presenter notes

Slide summary: Every gap is declared openly: land-use zones currently cover 4 sheets (1.5% of Greater Bengaluru) and the July 2025 amendment PDF is unobtained. Next: Bengaluru complete, Karnataka, other states with steward colleges, and the planned agent engine.

Presenter notes: Honesty about what is missing is just as important as what works today. Every gap in our pilot dataset is declared openly in `declarations.json` and shown on the Pilot page: land-use zone polygons currently cover 4 sheets in parts of Bengaluru South (1,276 zone polygons, 1.5% of Greater Bengaluru), with uncovered areas marked by a diagonal hatch on the map; the July 2025 zoning amendment PDF could not yet be obtained from public sources; the October 2024 Kannada compilation is unstructured in favour of the English original plus the 8 English amendments; and fire, TDR, NBC 2016, and aviation instruments are listed by reference. Our four-step roadmap takes us from completing Bengaluru's map sheets and workshops to Karnataka, other states, and shipping the planned local agent engine.

Opening · The Bylaw One Guide 1 / 24

Bengaluru's building rules. One code.

Bengaluru's building rules sit across 16 official instruments from 10 bodies. Bylaw One joins them into one open, cited, machine-readable code — 5,480 provisions, 271 rules as data, and 369 wards — current as of 14 May 2026.

Welcome to Bylaw One. Look at any building plot in Bengaluru: the rules that govern it are not in a single book. They sit across 16 in-force acts, building bye-laws, master plan zoning regulations, and gazette amendments issued by 10 bodies over twenty-two years. Bylaw One joins those official publications into one open, cited, machine-readable code. Today the working pilot covers 5,480 structured provisions, 271 governing parameter rules as data, 5 City Corporations, 369 official wards, and 1,276 georeferenced land-use zone polygons across 4 sheets (1.5% of Greater Bengaluru), verified by 10 automatic checks on every build.

01 / The Narrative 4 / 24

Why this exists

Building rules in India sit across overlapping PDFs from different bodies. Bylaw One turns them into one open, cited, machine-readable code so any person and any AI can answer "what may I build here?" with the official page behind it.

Here is the core problem we are solving. Every building in India is governed by rules scattered across bye-laws, master plans, amendments, circulars and state Acts, published as PDFs by different bodies, often contradicting each other. Architects, engineers, students and homeowners spend days finding which rule applies, and still aren't sure. Bylaw One turns those rules into one open, cited, machine-readable code, so that any person, and any AI they use, can answer "what may I build here?" with the exact official page behind every answer. It rests on three ideas: Open, Cited, and Collective — and ends with one habit: Read. Trace. Compare.

See it working

Four live views show Bylaw One working today: the five-step FAR story (2004 to today), a subject page showing what applies today first, the map Place Card with rules by zone, and a browser workshop verification task.

Fourth, the Verify page lets workshop participants compare a record side by side with the official PDF page and export a CSV verdict.

03 / Pipeline, Resolution, Map & AI 11 / 24

How it's built

Official PDFs pass through five deterministic layers — source register, verbatim structure, rules as data, six-step statutory resolution, and static web/AI endpoints — guarded by 10 automatic build checks and double-keyed human verification.

How do we turn scanned and digital government PDFs into a trustworthy code? Every release passes through five layers. First, the source register acquires each official PDF with its SHA-256 digest, Wayback Machine snapshot, and quoted commencement evidence. Second, the structure stage builds a faithful hierarchy of 5,480 active provisions with tables as structured rows and keeps editorial summaries strictly separate in `notes_by_site`. Third, parameter extraction turns tables into 271 active condition-bearing records with cell-level provenance. Fourth, a stated six-step statutory order settles overlaps across instruments while keeping older rules visible. Fifth, the build publishes the web reader, the 8-layer Protomaps/MapLibre map, and machine-readable endpoints (`/llms.txt`, `.md` pages, `/api/v1/` OpenAPI 3.1 JSON). Every build runs 10 automatic verification suites, and records become "Verified by a person" only after two independent workshop Match verdicts.

03 / Pipeline, Resolution, Map & AI · Diagram 13 / 24

The checks pipeline (10 automatic build checks + workshop verification)

Every build runs 10 automated checks against stored PDF page text and bounds; two independent human Match verdicts promote a record to person-verified.

Trust comes from two verification levels: Level 1 runs 10 automated checks on every build (text fidelity against stored PDF page text, hierarchy depth, parameter plausibility, band continuity, 5-corporation parity, map street-offset, provenance, plain language, licences, and WCAG AA budgets). Level 2 requires two independent workshop Match verdicts and zero Mismatches.
04 / Non-Negotiable Rules 14 / 24

Principles

Six principles govern every release: verbatim legal text with nothing added inside, every rule traced to its official and archived page, derived values labelled, disagreements settled by stated order, not legal advice, and permanent openness (Apache-2.0 and CC BY 4.0).

Every contributor, college steward, and AI integration in Bylaw One is bound by six plain principles. First, the law's words are shown exactly as printed, with nothing added inside legal text. Second, every rule is traced to its official page, with an archived copy. Third, anything the site works out — whether a consolidated provision, an extracted table row, or a 30-metre lake buffer — is explicitly labelled as derived. Fourth, when rules disagree, a stated order decides, and both rules stay visible; we show "not settled" when the law does not decide. Fifth, this is an open reference, not legal advice — always confirm with the authority. Sixth, released data and code stay open permanently under Apache-2.0 and CC BY 4.0.
05 / Roles, Layered Packs & State Stewards 15 / 24

The movement

Bylaw One is organised around four roles — State stewards, Contributors, Reviewers, and Maintainers — and a planned three-tier pack architecture (national, state, and city) that records whether each higher rule is adopted, adopted with changes, or reference only.

No single team can curate and verify the building rules of every Indian city alone. Bylaw One is organised as a collective movement across four clear roles: State stewards (colleges that curate their state's rules, verify records, and teach with them), Contributors (anyone proposing sources, corrections, or cities), Reviewers (faculty and practitioners who sign off verification), and Maintainers (the core team that runs the engine, data format, and checks). Bylaw One is run as a brand under the owner's organisation, and all released work stays open regardless. To scale across India without duplicating text, we have designed a planned layered pack architecture — national, state, and city — where shared text is stored once and each city pack records whether a state or national model rule was adopted, adopted with changes, or is reference only.

06 / Colleges, Students, Practitioners & Workshops 17 / 24

Take part

Colleges sign functional MoUs with semester workshops and internships; students gain practical skills, 60–120 hour internship credit, certificates, and named release credit; practitioners save hours and review rules; civic groups share open sources.

Why do colleges, students, practitioners, and civic groups take part? For colleges, accreditation counts functional MoUs — MoUs with real activity during the assessment period. Bylaw One's MoU comes with activities every semester: a one-day workshop, a faculty session, and supervised verification internships, plus a citable dataset and the state-steward role. For students, it builds skills employers want — reading city rules and checking AI answers against the gazette — along with 60 to 120-hour verification internships, certificates, named credit in every release, and a possible national student design trophy. For faculty, it provides publishable research and citable releases. For practitioners, it saves hours finding which rule applies, gives early access to the planned agent engine, and gives a voice in what comes next. Our one-day workshop runs in five hands-on sessions totaling four hours forty-five minutes, and is also offered as a two-hour faculty session.
07 / Architecture, Pipeline & Planned Agent Engine 18 / 24

For developers

The repository separates a Python data pipeline (`pipeline/`) from a static Next.js reader (`app/`) across 15 JSON Schemas (`schemas/`). A planned local TypeScript agent engine will expose four doors: MCP server, CLI, Agent Skill, and open data files.

For developers and technical contributors, the repository has a clean two-half architecture. The offline Python 3.12+ pipeline (`pipeline/`, managed with `uv`) acquires PDFs, parses tables, structures provisions, applies amendments, extracts parameters, georeferences map sheets, and validates outputs against fifteen Draft 2020-12 JSON Schemas in `schemas/`. The Next.js App Router frontend at the repository root (`app/`, `components/`, `lib/`) is a static, read-only reader with zero city-specific constants (Rule R1). We are also designing the planned local agent engine for the launch: one small TypeScript engine running on the user's own machine with separately updated data packs, offline keyword and meaning-based search, and four doors — a local MCP server, a CLI, an Agent Skill teaching the honesty rules, and the open data files themselves.

08 / Timeline, Public Launch & Cohorts 20 / 24

The launch

The launch roadmap runs from the quiet pilot and partner MoUs in December 2026 to the public launch and first student workshop in Bengaluru in the last week of January 2027, followed by the May–July "Verify Bengaluru" internship cohort.

Here is our launch timeline from late November 2026 through December 2027. Between 30 November and 6 December 2026, the trust round and pilot work merge, the partner kit is drafted, the launch host college is chosen, and first contact begins with the national students' architecture association about a student design trophy. From 7 to 20 December, Zenodo DOIs are switched on, the engine beta starts, and we run a quiet pilot with a handful of architects and faculty. After fixes, a demo video, and faculty sessions in early January, the public launch takes place in Bengaluru in the last week of January 2027 alongside the first student workshop, leading into the May–July "Verify Bengaluru" internship cohort and the December 2027 one-year report.
09 / Funding Model, Governance & Success Measures 21 / 24

Sustainability

The rules and code stay free and open permanently under Apache-2.0 and CC BY 4.0; income comes from around the data — grants, open sponsorships, firm training, integrations, CSR, and government projects — measured against transparent pilot-year goals.

How does Bylaw One stay sustainable while keeping the law free and open? The rules and source code stay open permanently under Apache-2.0 and CC BY 4.0; income comes from around the data. Early support comes from civic-technology grants and openly credited sponsorship of workshops, the student trophy, or a city's rules. Early-to-mid income comes from paid training for firms on reading the rules and using AI responsibly. Mid-term income comes from integrations and hosted endpoints with service guarantees, followed later by CSR funding and government projects built on the same open model. We track pilot-year progress openly, pairing stated goals with live numbers generated from the release.
10 / Declared Coverage Gaps & Roadmap 22 / 24

What's missing and what's next

Every gap is declared openly: land-use zones currently cover 4 sheets (1.5% of Greater Bengaluru) and the July 2025 amendment PDF is unobtained. Next: Bengaluru complete, Karnataka, other states with steward colleges, and the planned agent engine.

Honesty about what is missing is just as important as what works today. Every gap in our pilot dataset is declared openly in `declarations.json` and shown on the Pilot page: land-use zone polygons currently cover 4 sheets in parts of Bengaluru South (1,276 zone polygons, 1.5% of Greater Bengaluru), with uncovered areas marked by a diagonal hatch on the map; the July 2025 zoning amendment PDF could not yet be obtained from public sources; the October 2024 Kannada compilation is unstructured in favour of the English original plus the 8 English amendments; and fire, TDR, NBC 2016, and aviation instruments are listed by reference. Our four-step roadmap takes us from completing Bengaluru's map sheets and workshops to Karnataka, other states, and shipping the planned local agent engine.
